newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork bellies tumble on export forecast.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork bellies tumble on export forecast.

text.p: A downward adjustment by the USDA in its pork export projections knocked CME hog and pork belly futures to sharply lower closes, with pork bellies ending mostly down the three-cent-a-lb limit.

Hog futures closed 0.625 to 1.475 cent per lb lower paced by July at 79.350 cents. Pork bellies ended limit down in July through February contracts with March off 2.850 cents. February ended limit down at 78.900, two month lows.
General selling and long liquidation by commercials and funds combined to press hog futures from the start after the USDA Meat Supply and Use Forecast was released.
USDA lowered 1997 projected pork exports by 105 million lbs to 1.250 bllion lbs and lowered 1998 projections by 115 million lbs to 1.465 billion lbs.
The downward revision caught the market unprepared, especially as pork exports to Japan had been expected by many market watchers to rise sharply this summer, they said.

"The government is reversing gears and looking for lower numbers - I think that caught the market by surprise today and it's leading the market lower," said Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp.

Declines were curbed in June hogs which showed scaledown support ahead of its expiration on Friday and its relation to the CME lean hog index. Local short covering kept other months off lows late, traders added.
Rosenthal Collins and Rand Financials notably sold July at the start with ING and Dean Witter sellers on the break. Refco bought August and sold July late, pit sources said.

In hog options, LIT division of First Options bought August 76 puts. Iowa Grain was doing risk reversals, selling October 68 puts and buying 74 calls, selling December 64 puts and buying 70 calls and selling February 64 puts and buying 68 calls. RBH bought July 82 calls, pit sources added.

Pork belly futures sank the limit after early short-covering support as long liquidation touched off sell stops. Futures locked limit down by midsession and ended with 500 sell orders unsold in July and 150 unsold in August, traders said.
Weak cash product also weighed on the market. Wholesale cash belly prices have fallen to the mid $70's, the lowest levels since early May, some sources noted.
Sharp losses were seen continuing Friday as options closed synthetically lower.
July was at 77.500 cents, down another 1.400 cent and August at 78.000, down a further 1.175 cents, options traders said.
ADM Investor Services notably sold on the initial break, pit sources said.
